directly into ``<output>/`` (post flatten migration — no ``frames/``

  ``video-source``) — or ``builtin/video-array-source`` (``arrayed<video-source>``)
  when the "并行处理数组输入" checkbox is on. Each shard sees a directory
  containing one video.

  sequence (files ``frame_XXXXXX.png`` sit at the handle root, no
  ``frames/`` wrapper). Under arrayable_toggle the aggregate becomes
  ``arrayed<arrayed<image>>`` with ``dim_labels=[cam,frame]`` — outer
  = per-camera shard dir, inner = per-frame file.

  source-index window (half-open ``[start, end)``); ``skip`` is the
  stride *within* that window; ``max_frames`` is an absolute cap on
  the output count. All four mirror the STG ``pre_no_prior`` recipe.

  width preserving aspect ratio (never upscales). 0 = keep native.

(``frames-to-camera-track``) consumes this handle directly — no
re-extraction, no video decode.

output contract are unchanged. HEIC requires Pillow and pillow-heif in the
host Python environment (installed with HoloLab); missing imports fail clearly.

Non-HEIC images retain their exact filenames and remain symlinks.

RGB/RGBA pixels and alpha, with EXIF orientation baked into pixels.
All eight orientations are supported; output EXIF orientation is removed.

sequences are not exported. HDR above 8 bits fails explicitly rather than
silently reducing precision. PNG is lossless relative to decoded HEIC pixels.

original-name.heic.png (or .HEIC.png). Ambiguous fallback names fail explicitly.
Use a fresh output directory; failed runs may leave partial outputs.

packs.description: Run COLMAP Structure-from-Motion and emit a colmap-cams bundle plus a separate point-cloud output. Supports a shared camera, one camera per image folder, or one camera per image.
packs.docs:
Wrapper around the vanilla COLMAP CLI: ``feature_extractor`` +
``exhaustive_matcher`` + ``mapper``. With its defaults this is deliberately
command-equivalent to ``colmap-sfm@0.3.0``: all input images share one
OPENCV camera, COLMAP's 1.2 focal-length initialization is used, and focal
length / distortion are refined while the principal point remains fixed.

## Camera assignment

``camera_assignment`` controls COLMAP camera IDs, not image poses:

* ``single`` (default): one intrinsic shared by every image. This preserves
  the historical STG behaviour and is the safe default for monocular input.
* ``per_folder``: images in each immediate source folder share a camera.
  Use a source layout such as ``cam0/frame.jpg``, ``cam1/frame.jpg``.
* ``per_image``: every image gets an independent COLMAP camera ID. This is
  appropriate for a synchronized multi-device capture only when the devices
  really have different intrinsics.

``camera_model`` is passed directly to COLMAP. ``OPENCV`` remains the
compatibility default. For unconstrained per-image estimation prefer the
lower-dimensional ``SIMPLE_RADIAL`` model: it estimates focal length and one
radial coefficient while retaining COLMAP's image-centre principal point.
``default_focal_length_factor`` initializes focal length as this factor times
``max(width, height)`` when EXIF does not provide one. For a 4000 px image
with an expected 2760 px focal length, use ``0.69`` rather than COLMAP's
default ``1.2``.

## Identifiability boundary

``per_image`` makes COLMAP optimize separate camera parameter blocks; a low
reprojection error is **not** proof that fully free calibration is unique.
One exposure per device with a fully free 5-DOF intrinsic matrix and
independent distortion is commonly underconstrained / ill-conditioned and
admits multiple solutions. A restricted model (for example one focal length
per device, fixed principal point, simple distortion) with non-planar,
overlapping views and non-critical baselines can be jointly estimated, but
should still be checked across captures. Pure rotation, planar structure,
narrow baselines, and weak overlap are classic failure cases.

Recommended production pipeline: calibrate every physical device offline,
assign each device one COLMAP camera ID, inject its known camera parameters
into the database via COLMAP ``rig_configurator``, and pass those camera IDs
to ``--Mapper.constant_camera_list_path``. Then a single synchronized group
solves only poses and points. This pack does not yet accept a per-device
calibration JSON directly; use the COLMAP database/rig-configurator step
before mapper when calibrated intrinsics must be frozen.

Output layout::

    cams/ cameras.txt + images.txt
    points/ points3D.txt

packs.docs:
### IMAGE_ID integrity fix

The per-shard manual model preserves each matched image's IMAGE_ID from the
input SfM model. Previously the present subset was renumbered from 1, which
made point tracks incompatible with the original ``images.txt`` whenever an
intermediate rig camera was absent (for example ``1..5,7`` became ``1..6``).

### v0.7.5 — per-frame SIFT extraction controls

This pack owns the database used by its triangulation: it runs a fresh
``feature_extractor`` and ``exhaustive_matcher`` for every frame shard.
Consequently these SIFT controls affect the per-frame output here, not the
upstream ``colmap-sfm`` calibration database. Defaults reproduce COLMAP's
historical SIFT defaults and preserve the prior invocation behaviour.

### v0.7.4 — incomplete groups are valid shards

A shard uses the intersection of its staged files and SfM ``images.txt``.
Missing rig cameras are recorded in ``triangulation_meta.json`` and stdout;
fewer than two matched images fails explicitly.

### v0.7.3 — multi-intrinsic SfM input

``cams`` may contain one or more COLMAP camera rows. Each raw image uses

packs.description: Composite ordered video layers with per-layer transforms and start offsets.
packs.docs:
Consumes the whole array in one invocation (no fan-out). Non-dot entry names sort lexically; later layers are on top. Zero-pad numeric IDs. Each video element is one video file or a directory containing exactly one video.
Required transforms/offsets are paired with videos by position along the layer axis: independently sort each directory by non-dot entry name, then pair element 0 with 0, etc. Filenames need not match; video IDs are preserved. Both arrays must have exactly the video count. Each attribute leaf is a file. Hidden entries are ignored. No broadcasting or partial arrays.
float contract: one finite decimal number (scientific notation allowed), whitespace around it allowed. Offsets must be >= 0. vec3 contract: a JSON array of exactly three finite numbers [x_ratio, y_ratio, scale]; booleans/strings are invalid and scale must be > 0.
x/y are the layer's top-left relative to canvas width/height. Out-of-bounds content is clipped, never repositioned. First contain the display-aspect-correct layer in the canvas, then multiply both dimensions by scale; unlike overlay width_ratio, scale is NOT a fraction of canvas width.
Both transforms and offsets must be supplied explicitly; there are no position or start-time defaults. Each layer plays from source time 0 and disappears at its natural video-stream end; it never freezes or loops.
Canvas is the first layer's display size (rotation and SAR accounted for), padded to even. fps omitted/null uses the first layer's average frame rate (fallback nominal rate). Output is CFR; VFR sources are resampled. Total duration is max(offset + natural video duration), rounded UP to an output frame. Black canvas remains visible in gaps. fps override must be >0 and <=240.
CPU-only, two encoder/filter threads, env kiri. Silent H.264/yuv420p, CRF 20, faststart. Input media is never modified.

packs.description: Crop a rectangle from one image, or add a constant-color border.
packs.docs:
Four independent float paddings, always in pixels (never ratios).
Positive values remove pixels from that side; negative values add a border.
Round to nearest integer, with half pixels away from zero (0.5 -> 1).
Coordinates refer to stored pixels; no resizing, rotation or EXIF auto-orientation.
Output size: W - left - right by H - top - bottom after rounding.
Crop bounds are clamped to the original image. If positive paddings remove
all original pixels on either axis, fail clearly; outward padding cannot
rescue an empty crop. The retained rectangle must be at least 1x1.
PNG/JPEG/WebP encoding and sample bit depth are preserved; format is detected
from bytes, so extensionless file handles work. All-zero is a byte-for-byte copy.
JPEG crops are re-encoded at quality 95; WebP crops use lossless encoding.
PNG supports 16-bit samples without downconversion and indexed bit depths.
Indexed borders must use an existing opaque palette color or fail explicitly.
Low-bit grayscale may use an equivalent palette at the same bit depth.
pad_color is opaque #RRGGBB; grayscale uses luminance (16-bit scales by 257).
Animated images are rejected. Output limit: 100 million pixels, 100000 per side.

packs.docs:
### XMP preservation

JPEG outputs retain the input image's standard and Extended XMP APP1
segments byte-for-byte after OpenCV encoding. The transfer edits only JPEG
header segments and leaves the encoded scan untouched. EXIF is intentionally
not copied, preventing a stale Orientation tag from rotating already
undistorted pixels a second time.

### v0.5.2 — incomplete groups are valid shards

Single-image files and flat monocular image sets are also accepted. For
``blank_pixels=0``, the derived crop is checked against the forward
sampling border and tightened to avoid rounding/tangential black edges.

The output is the intersection of staged group images and SfM pose rows.
Missing cameras are reported in stdout and ``undistortion_meta.json`` in
the ``cams`` output; remaining cameras are undistorted normally.

### v0.5.1 — per-image intrinsic models

Accepts a COLMAP ``cams`` bundle with multiple camera rows.  The
``images.txt`` camera_id selects the source model for each image; OPENCV
and SIMPLE_RADIAL are converted independently to PINHOLE.  The classic
single-OPENCV path is retained.

### v0.5.0 — GPU rewrite

@0.4.1 shelled out to ``colmap image_undistorter``; that binary is a
heavily-threaded CPU pipeline (OpenMP + TBB + Ceres) that peaks at
~5 s solo per 21-image shard and stretches to ~18–26 s under 8-way
fan-out (`packs/image-undistort@0.4.1/manifest.yaml:66-75`). @0.5.0
keeps every bundle-level behavior identical and swaps the compute
path for one ``torch.nn.functional.grid_sample`` call over the whole
shard.

Pipeline (per shard):

1. Stage 21 image files into scratch (hardlink; identical to @0.4.1).
2. Copy the SfM sparse prior in and rewrite ``images.txt`` NAMEs to
   the staged basenames (identical to @0.4.1's ``stage_sparse_prior``).
3. Parse the single OPENCV camera row (fx fy cx cy k1 k2 p1 p2).
4. Derive PINHOLE ``new_K`` matching COLMAP's ``image_undistorter
   --blank_pixels 0``: sample all 4 borders with a 20-iter Newton on
   COLMAP's pixel-center convention (``u,v = 0.5 .. W-0.5, H-0.5``)
   to un-distort each border sample to normalized coordinates, take
   the largest inscribed axis-aligned rectangle, then **symmetrize
   about (0, 0)** (``min(|left|, |right|)`` and ``min(|top|, |bot|)``)
   so the principal point lands on the new-image center — matching
   COLMAP's ``cx_new = W_new/2 & cy_new = H_new/2`` invariant while
   keeping ``fx``/``fy`` unchanged.

   On a real 21-img OPENCV shard (2704×2028, tiny OPENCV distortion),
   this produces ``2688×2016 cx=1344.0 cy=1008.0`` — W matches
   COLMAP byte-for-byte, H off by 1 pixel from COLMAP's ``2688×2015
   cx=1344.0 cy=1007.5``. Reverse-engineering the last-pixel rounding
   would require reading the .cc side of ``image/undistortion.cc``
   (not shipped in the conda pkg headers), and the (K, image) pair is
   self-consistent either way — STG's downstream reader only checks
   ``model=="PINHOLE"``.
5. Decode the N images with cv2 in a 8-way thread pool (~600 ms for
   21 imgs on the box), upload as uint8 (4× less PCIe than float32),
   promote to float on the GPU, run one batched ``grid_sample``
   (bilinear, ``align_corners=True``, ``padding_mode=zeros``), cast
   to uint8, download. Pure kernel: ~6 ms for 21 imgs; total GPU
   roundtrip: ~600 ms dominated by H2D + D2H.
6. Encode PNGs with cv2 (``PNG_COMPRESSION=1``) in the same thread
   pool.
7. Emit ``cameras.txt`` (PINHOLE, COLMAP-format header) +
   ``images.txt`` (poses / IDs / observations preserved verbatim
   from the SfM prior; NAMEs rewritten to staged basenames) +
   empty ``points3D.txt`` on ``cams-out``. Emit the undistorted
   PNGs on ``images-out``.

#### Accuracy vs @0.4.1

Golden test on the shard used in @0.4.1's own benchmarks
(``w/3711480d-…/j/63469c73-…``, OPENCV 2704×2028, 21 cams):

* ``cameras.txt`` — **byte-identical** to COLMAP's output after
  symmetric-centering step 4c above.
* Pixel diff (21 imgs, RGB, 0–255): **RMSE=0.67, mean|d|=0.27,
  max|d|=41** (max is at a few high-frequency edge pixels; ≥97.9%
  within ±1 gray level). Source of the sub-pixel disagreement is
  GPU vs CPU bilinear floating-point rounding; STG's readers only
  check ``model=="PINHOLE"`` (``dataset_readers.py:156`` and 7
  parallel sites), so this is well inside the downstream tolerance.

#### Performance vs @0.4.1

Cold single-shard breakdown (fresh subprocess, GPU quiet):

* python + imports (torch 1.4 s, kornia 0.25 s, cv2/np 0.1 s): **~1.9 s**
* CUDA init (first tensor + sync): **~0.9 s**
* stage images + prior: ~25 ms
* read PNG (cv2 threaded ×8): ~700 ms
* build grid: ~100 ms
* GPU (fp16 chunk=8, pinned host out): ~270 ms
  (H2D 90 + permute+cast 10 + grid_sample+u8 50 + D2H 120)
* write PNG (cv2 threaded ×8, compress=1): ~930 ms
* publish cams.txt/images.txt: ~15 ms
* **total: ~4.5 s** (of which imports+CUDA ~2.8 s = 62 %)

Real 100-shard runs on the classic-STG workflow (same 21-img shards
~2704×2028), measured on the framework's own timings:

* ``@0.4.1`` CPU, ``parallelism=8``: p50 22.24 s, mean 25.55 s,
  max 423.78 s, **fan-out wall 423 s (7.06 min)**
* ``@0.5.0`` v1 (fp32, chunk=3, ``parallelism=4``): p50 6.89 s,
  mean 7.03 s, max 13.92 s, **fan-out wall 313 s (5.22 min)**
* ``@0.5.0`` v2 (fp16, chunk=8, ``parallelism=8``, pinned D2H):
  p50 11.34 s, mean 11.76 s, max 25.92 s, **fan-out wall 260 s
  (4.34 min)** — **1.63× speedup vs @0.4.1**

Notes:
* At ``parallelism=8`` each shard is ~1.7× slower than at
  ``parallelism=4`` (PCIe H2D/D2H + GPU kernel serialization split
  across 8 procs). Net wall still improves because 8/4 concurrency
  beats 1.7 slowdown.
* The remaining gap to ~1-2 min is dominated by (a) 2.8 s of
  per-shard cold-start (imports+CUDA context creation), and (b)
  ~1-2 s of framework overhead between shards per slot. Both need
  a persistent-worker mechanism (either pack-internal daemon or
  framework-level ``persistent: true``); the executor invariant is
  subprocess-per-shard (``hololab/node/executor.py:6`` "sacred
  boundary"), so this is out of scope for a pack-only change.

Tuning knobs:

* ``dtype`` (default ``fp16``): fp32 doubles VRAM; fp16 vs fp32 has
  RMSE 0.71 on 8-bit inputs — no visible quality loss for STG.
  bf16 rejected empirically (RMSE 4.65).
* ``chunk_size`` (default 8): peak VRAM ~1 GB / proc at fp16 chunk=8;
  fits 8-way concurrent on 24 GB with headroom. chunk=21 (whole shard
  in one kernel) OOMs at 8-way.
* ``png_compress`` (default 1): compress=0 saves ~330 ms/shard on
  encode but inflates output 4×; compress=1 matches COLMAP output
  size within a few %.
* ``io_workers`` (default 8): thread pool for cv2 PNG decode/encode.

#### Concurrency and thread caps

The GPU pack does not need @0.4.1's OMP env vars — no COLMAP process
runs, and torch/cv2 respect the OMP env if it happens to be set. The
exec preamble still sets ``OMP_NUM_THREADS=2`` to keep cv2's
``parallel_for_`` (TBB) and any transiently-touched Eigen paths from
hogging cores when the framework fans out multiple GPU pack invocations
in parallel.

#### Deviations from @0.4.1 to be aware of

* ``--blank-pixels`` accepts 0 (inscribed) and 1 (bounding). COLMAP
  supports fractional values in [0, 1] that linearly interpolate
  between the two rects; this pack implements only the two
  endpoints. In-repo workflows all use 0.
* COLMAP's ``max_image_size`` / ``min_scale`` / ``max_scale`` /
  ROI knobs are not exposed. None are used by in-repo workflows.
* Output PNGs are re-encoded by cv2 (libpng) rather than COLMAP
  (also libpng under the hood). Byte size within a few percent;
  downstream STG reads pixels, not file bytes.

Everything else — staging shape, NAME rewrite bridge via
``sfm_key``, output layout on ``cams-out``/``images-out``, sparse-
prior handling, blank-pixels default — matches @0.4.1.

header segments and leaves the encoded scan untouched. EXIF is intentionally
not copied, preventing a stale Orientation tag from rotating already
undistorted pixels a second time.

### v0.5.2 — incomplete groups are valid shards

Single-image files and flat monocular image sets are also accepted. For
``blank_pixels=0``, the derived crop is checked against the forward
sampling border and tightened to avoid rounding/tangential black edges.

The output is the intersection of staged group images and SfM pose rows.
Missing cameras are reported in stdout and ``undistortion_meta.json`` in
the ``cams`` output; remaining cameras are undistorted normally.

### v0.5.4 — additional COLMAP camera models

``SIMPLE_PINHOLE`` and ``PINHOLE`` are accepted as zero-distortion OPENCV
equivalents. ``RADIAL`` is also accepted as the two-radial-coefficient
OPENCV subset. Unsupported models, including fisheye and ``FULL_OPENCV``,
fail with the model name, supplied parameter count, and supported-model
list.

### v0.5.1 — per-image intrinsic models

Accepts a COLMAP ``cams`` bundle with multiple camera rows.  The
``images.txt`` camera_id selects the source model for each image; OPENCV
and SIMPLE_RADIAL are converted independently to PINHOLE.  The classic
single-OPENCV path is retained.

### v0.5.0 — GPU rewrite

@0.4.1 shelled out to ``colmap image_undistorter``; that binary is a
heavily-threaded CPU pipeline (OpenMP + TBB + Ceres) that peaks at
~5 s solo per 21-image shard and stretches to ~18–26 s under 8-way
fan-out (`packs/image-undistort@0.4.1/manifest.yaml:66-75`). @0.5.0
keeps every bundle-level behavior identical and swaps the compute
path for one ``torch.nn.functional.grid_sample`` call over the whole
shard.

Pipeline (per shard):

1. Stage 21 image files into scratch (hardlink; identical to @0.4.1).
2. Copy the SfM sparse prior in and rewrite ``images.txt`` NAMEs to
   the staged basenames (identical to @0.4.1's ``stage_sparse_prior``).
3. Parse the single OPENCV camera row (fx fy cx cy k1 k2 p1 p2).
4. Derive PINHOLE ``new_K`` matching COLMAP's ``image_undistorter
   --blank_pixels 0``: sample all 4 borders with a 20-iter Newton on
   COLMAP's pixel-center convention (``u,v = 0.5 .. W-0.5, H-0.5``)
   to un-distort each border sample to normalized coordinates, take
   the largest inscribed axis-aligned rectangle, then **symmetrize
   about (0, 0)** (``min(|left|, |right|)`` and ``min(|top|, |bot|)``)
   so the principal point lands on the new-image center — matching
   COLMAP's ``cx_new = W_new/2 & cy_new = H_new/2`` invariant while
   keeping ``fx``/``fy`` unchanged.

   On a real 21-img OPENCV shard (2704×2028, tiny OPENCV distortion),
   this produces ``2688×2016 cx=1344.0 cy=1008.0`` — W matches
   COLMAP byte-for-byte, H off by 1 pixel from COLMAP's ``2688×2015
   cx=1344.0 cy=1007.5``. Reverse-engineering the last-pixel rounding
   would require reading the .cc side of ``image/undistortion.cc``
   (not shipped in the conda pkg headers), and the (K, image) pair is
   self-consistent either way — STG's downstream reader only checks
   ``model=="PINHOLE"``.
5. Decode the N images with cv2 in a 8-way thread pool (~600 ms for
   21 imgs on the box), upload as uint8 (4× less PCIe than float32),
   promote to float on the GPU, run one batched ``grid_sample``
   (bilinear, ``align_corners=True``, ``padding_mode=zeros``), cast
   to uint8, download. Pure kernel: ~6 ms for 21 imgs; total GPU
   roundtrip: ~600 ms dominated by H2D + D2H.
6. Encode PNGs with cv2 (``PNG_COMPRESSION=1``) in the same thread
   pool.
7. Emit ``cameras.txt`` (PINHOLE, COLMAP-format header) +
   ``images.txt`` (poses / IDs / observations preserved verbatim
   from the SfM prior; NAMEs rewritten to staged basenames) +
   empty ``points3D.txt`` on ``cams-out``. Emit the undistorted
   PNGs on ``images-out``.

#### Accuracy vs @0.4.1

Golden test on the shard used in @0.4.1's own benchmarks
(``w/3711480d-…/j/63469c73-…``, OPENCV 2704×2028, 21 cams):

* ``cameras.txt`` — **byte-identical** to COLMAP's output after
  symmetric-centering step 4c above.
* Pixel diff (21 imgs, RGB, 0–255): **RMSE=0.67, mean|d|=0.27,
  max|d|=41** (max is at a few high-frequency edge pixels; ≥97.9%
  within ±1 gray level). Source of the sub-pixel disagreement is
  GPU vs CPU bilinear floating-point rounding; STG's readers only
  check ``model=="PINHOLE"`` (``dataset_readers.py:156`` and 7
  parallel sites), so this is well inside the downstream tolerance.

#### Performance vs @0.4.1

Cold single-shard breakdown (fresh subprocess, GPU quiet):

* python + imports (torch 1.4 s, kornia 0.25 s, cv2/np 0.1 s): **~1.9 s**
* CUDA init (first tensor + sync): **~0.9 s**
* stage images + prior: ~25 ms
* read PNG (cv2 threaded ×8): ~700 ms
* build grid: ~100 ms
* GPU (fp16 chunk=8, pinned host out): ~270 ms
  (H2D 90 + permute+cast 10 + grid_sample+u8 50 + D2H 120)
* write PNG (cv2 threaded ×8, compress=1): ~930 ms
* publish cams.txt/images.txt: ~15 ms
* **total: ~4.5 s** (of which imports+CUDA ~2.8 s = 62 %)

Real 100-shard runs on the classic-STG workflow (same 21-img shards
~2704×2028), measured on the framework's own timings:

* ``@0.4.1`` CPU, ``parallelism=8``: p50 22.24 s, mean 25.55 s,
  max 423.78 s, **fan-out wall 423 s (7.06 min)**
* ``@0.5.0`` v1 (fp32, chunk=3, ``parallelism=4``): p50 6.89 s,
  mean 7.03 s, max 13.92 s, **fan-out wall 313 s (5.22 min)**
* ``@0.5.0`` v2 (fp16, chunk=8, ``parallelism=8``, pinned D2H):
  p50 11.34 s, mean 11.76 s, max 25.92 s, **fan-out wall 260 s
  (4.34 min)** — **1.63× speedup vs @0.4.1**

Notes:
* At ``parallelism=8`` each shard is ~1.7× slower than at
  ``parallelism=4`` (PCIe H2D/D2H + GPU kernel serialization split
  across 8 procs). Net wall still improves because 8/4 concurrency
  beats 1.7 slowdown.
* The remaining gap to ~1-2 min is dominated by (a) 2.8 s of
  per-shard cold-start (imports+CUDA context creation), and (b)
  ~1-2 s of framework overhead between shards per slot. Both need
  a persistent-worker mechanism (either pack-internal daemon or
  framework-level ``persistent: true``); the executor invariant is
  subprocess-per-shard (``hololab/node/executor.py:6`` "sacred
  boundary"), so this is out of scope for a pack-only change.

Tuning knobs:

* ``dtype`` (default ``fp16``): fp32 doubles VRAM; fp16 vs fp32 has
  RMSE 0.71 on 8-bit inputs — no visible quality loss for STG.
  bf16 rejected empirically (RMSE 4.65).
* ``chunk_size`` (default 8): peak VRAM ~1 GB / proc at fp16 chunk=8;
  fits 8-way concurrent on 24 GB with headroom. chunk=21 (whole shard
  in one kernel) OOMs at 8-way.
* ``png_compress`` (default 1): compress=0 saves ~330 ms/shard on
  encode but inflates output 4×; compress=1 matches COLMAP output
  size within a few %.
* ``io_workers`` (default 8): thread pool for cv2 PNG decode/encode.

#### Concurrency and thread caps

The GPU pack does not need @0.4.1's OMP env vars — no COLMAP process
runs, and torch/cv2 respect the OMP env if it happens to be set. The
exec preamble still sets ``OMP_NUM_THREADS=2`` to keep cv2's
``parallel_for_`` (TBB) and any transiently-touched Eigen paths from
hogging cores when the framework fans out multiple GPU pack invocations
in parallel.

#### Deviations from @0.4.1 to be aware of

* ``--blank-pixels`` accepts 0 (inscribed) and 1 (bounding). COLMAP
  supports fractional values in [0, 1] that linearly interpolate
  between the two rects; this pack implements only the two
  endpoints. In-repo workflows all use 0.
* COLMAP's ``max_image_size`` / ``min_scale`` / ``max_scale`` /
  ROI knobs are not exposed. None are used by in-repo workflows.
* Output PNGs are re-encoded by cv2 (libpng) rather than COLMAP
  (also libpng under the hood). Byte size within a few percent;
  downstream STG reads pixels, not file bytes.

Everything else — staging shape, NAME rewrite bridge via
``sfm_key``, output layout on ``cams-out``/``images-out``, sparse-
prior handling, blank-pixels default — matches @0.4.1.

### Track integrity

Preserve images.txt observation rows when rewriting names. Check each track
against its IMAGE_ID, POINT2D_IDX bounds and reciprocal POINT3D_ID. Invalid
indices or nonreciprocal observations fail before invoking COLMAP. BIN conversion remains mandatory
and fatal on failure, preserving compatibility with binary-only loaders.

### v0.4.0 vs v0.3.0

Type-system cleanup: the ``folder`` output tag list drops the
legacy ``colmap`` alias. ``@0.3.0`` shipped
``tags: [colmap-folder, colmap]`` so the edge into
``stg-train@0.2.0.colmap_frames`` (which declared ``[colmap]``)
would still validate without a manifest bump on the consumer side.
That was always a compat hack — one semantic type should surface
as one tag on the wire, not two aliases. ``stg-train@0.3.0``
declares ``colmap-folder`` on its input port and consumes the
``@0.4.0`` output directly.

Existing chains that used ``@0.3.0`` with the alias keep working
against ``stg-train@0.2.0`` — this bump is opt-in, not a rug pull.
New graphs should wire ``@0.4.0`` → ``stg-train@0.3.0``.

* ``cams``   — fan-out participant, ``arrayed<colmap-cams>[frame]``

               Each shard sees one per-frame point cloud.
* ``images`` — **optional** fan-out participant,
               ``arrayed<image>[frame]``. Wire for Mode B (with
               ``images/`` in the output); leave unwired for Mode A
               (sparse-only). Should typically be wired to the same
               und's ``images`` output so files match cams' images.txt
               NAMEs.

### Outputs

``folder`` — per-shard ``colmap-folder``; scalar per invocation,
wrap-dim ``["frame"]``; framework aggregates into
``arrayed<colmap-folder>[frame]``.

The script rewrites images.txt NAMEs to flat basenames matching the
actual per-cam files under ``images/``. Not strictly required when
cams comes from ``image-undistort@0.4.0`` (that pack already
rewrites NAMEs), but the code path is preserved so this pack still
works when cams comes straight from SfM.
